notes: Re-picked in verification. The writer's edit (asymmetric 'lies upstream of' made symmetric) had a delete that did not hold: asymmetry of 'lies upstream of' also follows from its transitivity and irreflexivity (no place lies upstream of itself), so deleting it alone leaves it derivable, the RBox form of the derived-beliefs problem. Symmetry of 'borders' follows from no other property, so its delete is clean. The edit swaps a true property (symmetric) for its opposite (asymmetric), the README's own RBox example. The questions ask 'does it follow that ... does not border ...', so the original answers are no and the new answers yes, keeping the topic's yes/no balance. The instances are true and undisputed (France-Spain, Brazil-Argentina). The zh prompt uses 毗邻 rather than 接壤, which reads as mutual by itself. Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
